/// A linear schedule destroys the signal too early: by the middle of the trajectory there is
/// little left to learn from, so half the model's capacity goes to steps that are already noise.
/// The cosine schedule keeps signal alive much longer, and for motion - where the interesting
/// structure is temporal and fine - it is the one that works.
pub fn betaSchedule(comptime T: type, betas: []T, kind: NoiseSchedule) Error!void {
    comptime requireFloat(T);
    if (betas.len < 2) {
        return Error.DomainError;
    }
    const steps: T = @floatFromInt(betas.len);
    switch (kind) {
        .linear => {
            // The endpoints are the values every implementation uses at T=1000, scaled so a
            // shorter schedule covers the same total noise rather than a fraction of it.
            const first: T = 1.0e-4 * (1000.0 / steps);
            const last: T = 0.02 * (1000.0 / steps);
            for (betas, 0..) |*b, i| {
                const at: T = @as(T, @floatFromInt(i)) / (steps - 1);
                b.* = first + (last - first) * at;
            }
        },
        .cosine => {
            // Defined through the cumulative product rather than directly: the schedule says
            // what fraction of the SIGNAL survives to step t, and the betas are read back out of
            // that. `s = 0.008` offsets the start so beta[0] is not exactly zero.
            const offset: T = 0.008;
            var previous: T = 1;
            for (betas, 0..) |*b, i| {
                const at: T = @as(T, @floatFromInt(i + 1)) / steps;
                const quarter_turn: T = @as(T, zm.pi) / 2;
                const angle: T = ((at + offset) / (1 + offset)) * quarter_turn;
                const c: T = zm.cosRad(angle);
                const bar: T = c * c;
                // Clamped at 0.999: the last few steps of a cosine schedule would otherwise ask
                // for a beta of essentially 1, and a variance of one leaves nothing for the
                // reverse step to work with.
                b.* = scalarClamp(1 - bar / previous, 0, 0.999);
                previous = bar;
            }
        },
    }
}
alphasCumprod
/// The cumulative signal fraction: `alpha_bar[t] = prod(1 - beta[0..=t])`.
///
/// ---- COMPUTED ONCE AND KEPT ----
///
/// Everything downstream needs this, not the betas: the forward process is
/// `sqrt(alpha_bar)*x0 + sqrt(1 - alpha_bar)*noise`, and each sampling step needs `alpha_bar` at
/// two timesteps. Recomputing the product inside a sampling loop makes generation quadratic in
/// the number of steps for no reason.
pub fn alphasCumprod(comptime T: type, out: []T, betas: []const T) Error!void {
    comptime requireFloat(T);
    if (out.len != betas.len or betas.len == 0) {
        return Error.ShapeMismatch;
    }
    var running: T = 1;
    for (out, betas) |*slot, beta| {
        if (beta < 0 or beta >= 1) {
            return Error.DomainError;
        }
        running *= 1 - beta;
        slot.* = running;
    }
}

beta[t] is how much variance step t adds. alpha_bar[t] is what accumulates: the fraction of the original signal still present after t steps, falling from nearly 1 to nearly 0.

That curve is a statement about where the model spends its capacity. Steps where alpha_bar is high are nearly clean, and teach fine detail; steps where it is low are nearly pure noise, and teach coarse structure. A schedule that falls too fast spends half the trajectory on samples that are already noise, and there is nothing left to learn from.

That is the difference between the two kinds. Linear destroys the signal early; cosine keeps it alive well past the midpoint. For motion — where the interesting structure is temporal and fine — cosine is the one that works.

Compute alpha_bar once and keep it. Every sampling step needs it at two timesteps, and rebuilding a cumulative product inside the loop makes generation quadratic in the step count for no reason.

17c.2 The forward process#

const noised = zn.addNoise(f64, clean, noise, alpha_bar[t]);
addNoise
/// The forward process: mix a clean sample with noise at a given timestep.
///
/// `sqrt(alpha_bar)*x0 + sqrt(1 - alpha_bar)*noise`. The two coefficients are the sine and cosine
/// of the same angle in effect - their squares sum to one - so the result has the same variance
/// as the input whatever the timestep. That is what lets one model handle every step: the scale
/// of its input does not drift.
pub fn addNoise(comptime T: type, x0: T, noise: T, alpha_bar: T) T {
    comptime requireFloat(T);
    return @sqrt(alpha_bar) * x0 + @sqrt(1 - alpha_bar) * noise;
}

That is sqrt(alpha_bar)*x0 + sqrt(1 - alpha_bar)*noise — a blend between the sample and pure noise, weighted so that the two coefficients square to one.

That detail is why a single network can handle every timestep: a unit-variance input stays unit-variance whatever t is. Get the weighting wrong and the scale of the model's input drifts across the trajectory, so the network sees a different problem at each end.

Notice there is no loop. Training does not walk the chain step by step — it jumps straight to a random timestep, because alpha_bar already encodes the whole prefix of the process. That is what makes training a diffusion model affordable.

17c.3 Noise or sample: two ways to say the same thing#

A model is trained to predict one of two things from a noised input: the noise that was added, or the clean sample underneath. They carry identical information, and the sampling loops need whichever you did not predict.

const eps = zn.epsilonFromX0(f64, noised, predicted_clean, alpha_bar[t]);
epsilonFromX0
/// Recover the noise that must have been added, given a prediction of the clean sample.
///
/// Models are trained to predict one of two equivalent things - the noise, or the original
/// sample - and the sampling loops need whichever they were not given. This is the conversion,
/// read straight off the forward process.
pub fn epsilonFromX0(comptime T: type, x_t: T, x0: T, alpha_bar: T) T {
    comptime requireFloat(T);
    return (x_t - @sqrt(alpha_bar) * x0) / @sqrt(1 - alpha_bar);
}

This is the forward process rearranged, nothing more. It is worth having as a named function because the rearrangement is where alpha gets used in place of alpha_bar, or a square root goes missing — and the result of either is samples that come out blurry rather than wrong. Blurry is indistinguishable from undertrained, which makes it an expensive mistake to chase.

17c.4 Generating: one step, two samplers#

Generation starts from pure noise and walks the schedule backwards, asking the model at each step what noise it sees and stepping toward a slightly cleaner sample.

var x = starting_noise;
var t = alpha_bar.len - 1;
while (t > 0) : (t -= 1) {
    const eps = model_prediction(x, t);
    x = zn.diffusionReverseStep(f64, x, eps, alpha_bar[t], alpha_bar[t - 1], eta, fresh_noise);
}
diffusionReverseStep
/// One reverse step: from `x_t` toward `x_{t-1}`, given the model's noise prediction.
///
/// Named for what it DOES rather than for one of the two samplers it implements. Calling it
/// `ddimStep` would have been the obvious choice and would have contradicted its own
/// documentation two lines down - DDIM is `eta = 0`, DDPM is `eta = 1`, and neither has a better
/// claim on the name than the other.
///
/// ---- DDPM AND DDIM ARE ONE UPDATE WITH A PARAMETER ----
///
/// They are usually presented as two samplers and implemented as two objects. They are not: both
/// take the same step and differ only in how much fresh noise they inject, which is exactly what
/// `eta` controls.
///
///   eta = 0   DDIM. Fully deterministic - the same starting noise always produces the same
///             sample, and the trajectory can skip timesteps, which is why DDIM samples in 50
///             steps where DDPM needs 1000.
///   eta = 1   DDPM. The original stochastic chain.
///
/// Anything between is a valid sampler, trading diversity against speed.
///
/// ---- WHAT THE THREE TERMS ARE ----
///
/// Estimate the clean sample from where we are and what the model thinks the noise was. Then
/// step back onto the trajectory at `t-1`: partly by re-noising that estimate along the SAME
/// direction the model identified, partly with fresh randomness.
///
///   sqrt(alpha_bar_prev) * x0     the estimate, scaled to the signal level at t-1
///   sqrt(1 - a_prev - s^2) * eps  the deterministic part, pointing the way the model said
///   sigma * fresh                 the stochastic part, zero when eta is zero
///
/// The middle term's coefficient shrinks by exactly the variance the third term adds, so the
/// total stays on the trajectory whatever `eta` is. That is the identity that makes one function
/// able to be both samplers.
pub fn diffusionReverseStep(
    comptime T: type,
    x_t: T,
    epsilon: T,
    alpha_bar_t: T,
    alpha_bar_prev: T,
    eta: T,
    fresh_noise: T,
) T {
    comptime requireFloat(T);
    const x0: T = x0FromEpsilon(T, x_t, epsilon, alpha_bar_t);

    // How much of the step is randomness. The `1 - a_t/a_prev` factor is the variance the
    // forward process added between the two timesteps - so at eta = 1 the step injects exactly
    // what the chain removed, which is what makes DDPM the special case rather than the default.
    const variance_ratio: T = (1 - alpha_bar_prev) / (1 - alpha_bar_t);
    const step_variance: T = 1 - alpha_bar_t / alpha_bar_prev;
    const sigma: T = eta * @sqrt(@max(variance_ratio * step_variance, 0));

    // Clamped at zero because `sigma^2` can exceed `1 - a_prev` by rounding at eta = 1, and a
    // negative under the root would give a NaN at the very last step of a chain that was
    // otherwise finished.
    const direction: T = @sqrt(@max(1 - alpha_bar_prev - sigma * sigma, 0)) * epsilon;
    return @sqrt(alpha_bar_prev) * x0 + direction + sigma * fresh_noise;
}

DDPM and DDIM are usually described as two samplers. They are one update with a parameter — eta is how much fresh randomness enters each step:

etasamplerbehaviour
0DDIMdeterministic; the same starting noise always gives the same sample, and steps can be skipped
1DDPMthe original stochastic chain

That is why DDIM can sample in 50 steps where DDPM needs 1000: with no randomness injected, the trajectory is a path you can take in larger strides. Values between the two are valid samplers trading diversity against speed.

What the step is doing

Three terms. Estimate the clean sample from where you are and what the model says the noise was. Then step back onto the trajectory at t-1: partly by re-noising that estimate along the direction the model identified, partly with fresh randomness.

The deterministic term's coefficient shrinks by exactly the variance the random term adds, so the step stays on the trajectory whatever eta is. That balance is why one function can be both samplers rather than two that merely resemble each other.

The property that defines a correct step

If the model's noise prediction were exactly right, a deterministic step from x_t would land exactly where the forward process puts x_{t-1} for the same clean sample and the same noise. The reverse step is the forward one run backwards, with no error at all.

That makes it an identity rather than an approximation, which is useful when something goes wrong: if a sampler drifts, the model's predictions are at fault, not the step.

17c.5 Telling the model which step it is on#

One network handles every step of the chain, and it has to behave differently at each — near the end it is removing a whisper of noise, near the start it is inventing structure from nothing. So the timestep is an input.

Feeding it as a single number makes that dependence something the network must learn from one scalar, and neighbouring timesteps look nearly identical to it. Instead, encode it:

var code: [128]f64 = undefined;
try zn.sinusoidalEmbedding(f64, &code, @floatFromInt(t), 10000.0);
sinusoidalEmbedding
/// Encode a timestep as a vector of sinusoids at geometrically spaced frequencies.
///
/// ---- WHY A NUMBER IS NOT ENOUGH ----
///
/// A diffusion model has to behave differently at every step of the chain - near the end it is
/// removing a whisper of noise, near the start it is inventing structure from nothing. Feeding
/// the timestep in as a single scalar makes that dependence something the network has to learn
/// from one input, and neighbouring timesteps look almost identical to it.
///
/// A sinusoidal code gives it timesteps that are FAR APART in the input whenever they should
/// behave differently, and close when they should not. The geometric spread of frequencies is
/// what covers both scales at once: the fastest components separate adjacent steps, the slowest
/// distinguish the beginning of the chain from the end.
///
/// ---- THE SAME CODE IS USED FOR POSITION ----
///
/// This is the transformer's positional encoding with a timestep in place of an index. Nothing
/// about it is diffusion-specific, which is why it is one function rather than two.
pub fn sinusoidalEmbedding(
    comptime T: type,
    out: []T,
    position: T,
    max_period: T,
) Error!void {
    comptime requireFloat(T);
    if (out.len < 2 or out.len % 2 != 0) {
        return Error.ShapeMismatch;
    }
    if (max_period <= 1) {
        return Error.DomainError;
    }
    const half: usize = out.len / 2;
    const log_period: T = @log(max_period);
    for (0..half) |i| {
        // Geometric, not linear: frequencies from 1 down to 1/max_period. A linear spread would
        // crowd every component into the same scale and waste most of the width.
        const share: T = @as(T, @floatFromInt(i)) / @as(T, @floatFromInt(half));
        const frequency: T = @exp(-log_period * share);
        const angle: T = position * frequency;
        // Cosines first, then sines - the pairing matters only in that it is CONSISTENT, since
        // the network learns whatever layout it is given. Split halves rather than interleaved
        // because it makes a slice of the first half a usable coarse code on its own.
        out[i] = zm.cosRad(angle);
        out[half + i] = zm.sinRad(angle);
    }
}

Sinusoids at geometrically spaced frequencies. The fast components separate adjacent steps; the slow ones distinguish the beginning of the chain from the end. Timesteps that should behave differently are far apart in the input, and ones that should not are close.

The same function is a transformer's positional encoding with an index in place of a timestep — nothing about it is diffusion-specific.

How the condition reaches the network

The obvious route — concatenate the embedding onto the input — makes it one more thing competing for attention among the tokens. AdaLayerNorm instead lets the condition set the scale and offset of every normalised activation, which reaches the whole layer at once:

const h = try graph.adaptiveLayerNorm(x, conditioning_gain, conditioning_bias, 1.0e-5);

The gain applied is 1 + conditioning_gain, and that 1 + is what lets the block train from scratch. A zero-initialised projection is then the identity: the block passes its input through untouched and the condition does nothing, rather than multiplying everything by zero and destroying the signal before any gradient has arrived.

The same mechanism conditions a policy on a goal or a latent skill, which is why it is a general tape operation rather than diffusion-specific.

17c.6 Guidance and the sampling average#

A conditional model tends to under-use its condition: it can lower its training loss by modelling the data well and the condition loosely. Classifier-free guidance fixes that at sampling time. Run the model twice — once with the condition, once without — and extrapolate along the difference.

const guided = zn.classifierFreeGuidance(f64, with_condition, without_condition, strength);
classifierFreeGuidance
/// Classifier-free guidance: push a conditional prediction away from an unconditional one.
///
/// ---- WHAT IT BUYS ----
///
/// A conditional model trained on (condition, sample) pairs tends to under-use the condition -
/// it can lower its loss by modelling the data well and the condition loosely. Guidance fixes
/// that at SAMPLING time rather than training time: run the model twice, once with the condition
/// and once without, and extrapolate along the difference.
///
///   strength = 0   the conditional prediction, unchanged
///   strength = 1   also unchanged - the terms cancel
///   strength > 1   exaggerate whatever the condition contributed
///
/// Typical values are 2 to 8. Too high and the samples become caricatures of the condition:
/// sharper, less diverse, and eventually unnatural - which is the trade the parameter exists to
/// expose rather than hide.
pub fn classifierFreeGuidance(
    comptime T: type,
    conditional: T,
    unconditional: T,
    strength: T,
) T {
    comptime requireFloat(T);
    return unconditional + strength * (conditional - unconditional);
}

Both 0 and 1 are fixed points: at 0 you get the unconditional prediction, at 1 the conditional one unchanged. Only beyond 1 does anything happen, and typical values are 2 to 8. Push it too far and samples become caricatures of the condition — sharper, less diverse, eventually unnatural.

Sample from the average, not the weights

try zn.emaUpdate(f64, shadow_weights, live_weights, 0.999);
emaUpdate
/// Move `shadow` a fraction `1 - decay` of the way toward `live`.
///
/// ---- THIS IS `polyakUpdate` UNDER THE NAME ITS OTHER USERS KNOW ----
///
/// A diffusion model samples from an exponential moving average of its weights rather than the
/// weights themselves, because the EMA is markedly less noisy than any single step of training.
/// An RL target network follows its online network the same way. **Identical arithmetic, two
/// vocabularies** - so this is an alias, not a second implementation.
///
/// ---- THE ARGUMENT IS THE COMPLEMENT, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS EXISTS ----
///
/// `polyakUpdate` takes `follow`, the small number: 0.005 means "move half a percent of the way".
/// EMA literature quotes `decay`, the large one: 0.999 means "keep 99.9% of what you had". They
/// describe the same update and **differ by exactly 1**, so passing one where the other is
/// expected gives a shadow that either tracks instantly or never moves - and both look like a
/// working system that learns badly.
pub fn emaUpdate(
    comptime T: type,
    shadow: Tensor(T),
    live: Tensor(T),
    decay: T,
) Error!void {
    comptime requireFloat(T);
    if (decay < 0 or decay > 1) {
        return Error.DomainError;
    }
    return polyakUpdate(T, shadow, live, 1 - decay);
}

Diffusion models generate from an exponential moving average of their weights rather than the weights themselves, because the average is markedly less noisy than any single point in training. An RL target network follows its online network the same way — identical arithmetic, two vocabularies — so emaUpdate is an alias for polyakUpdate rather than a second implementation.

The argument is the complement. polyakUpdate takes follow, the small number: 0.005 means “move half a percent of the way”. EMA literature quotes decay, the large one: 0.999 means “keep 99.9% of what you had”. They describe the same update and differ by exactly 1, so passing one where the other belongs gives a shadow that either tracks instantly or never moves — and both look like a working system that simply learns badly.

18.5 Running on the GPU#

zimrnum compiles to SPIR-V, so a kernel can call the same function the CPU does rather than restating it. The pattern is three lines in build.zig and one in the kernel:

// build.zig: mark the kernel module as wanting zimrnum
.wants_zimrnum = true,

// the kernel: call the host function directly
pub fn cartpole_step(c: k.Ctx(@This())) void {
    if (c.id >= c.params.count) return;
    state[c.id] = zrl.cartpoleStep(state[c.id], action[c.id], dt);
}
cartpoleStep
/// The cart-and-pole control benchmark: push a cart left or right to keep a pole upright.
///
/// A PURE FUNCTION - THE STATE GOES IN AND THE NEXT STATE COMES OUT
///
/// The step is PURE: a state in, the next state out. A step that updated its state in place would
/// make every rollout copy the observation out BEFORE calling it; forgetting would produce a rollout
/// whose observations are all one step late, which trains and converges to something slightly
/// wrong.
///
/// Returning the next state makes it unforgettable. It also makes the step replayable - the same
/// state and action give the same answer, always - which is what a test needs and what a
/// debugger needs.
///
/// RESET IS A SEPARATE FUNCTION, AND THAT REMOVES TWO FLAGS
///
/// Starting an episode is its own call: `cartpoleReset` gives a state, and `cartpoleStep` only ever
/// steps. A reset folded into the step would need a `force_reset` parameter, and then a
/// `no_transition` special case, because a forced reset produces no reward and no termination.
///
/// RADIANS HERE, AND THE SUFFIX SAYS SO - BECAUSE THIS ANGLE IS DIFFERENTIATED
///
/// The rest of this codebase moved to turns, and for geometry that was right: a quarter turn is
/// exactly 0.25, and `sinTurns` is exact where `sin(tau/4)` is not.
///
/// **A differentiated angle is the other case.** `d/dtheta sin(theta)` is `cos(theta)` only in
/// radians; in turns it is `tau * cos`, and every derivative in a dynamics system picks up that
/// factor. The cartpole equations are differential equations, so radians are the unit in which
/// they have no constants in them at all.
///
/// The first version of this held the pole in turns and converted the angular acceleration from
/// radians on the way in. That conversion was a place to be wrong, and I was: **the pole fell tau
/// times too fast** and every sign still looked right. Choosing the unit the equations are
/// written in removes the conversion rather than fixing it.
///
/// So: **turns for angles that are drawn, radians for angles that are differentiated**, and the
/// name carries the unit either way. `pole_rad` cannot be mistaken for `pole_turns`.
///
/// The limit is not a rounded constant: `radFromDeg(12)` is twelve degrees exactly as far as the
/// type can express it, where a literal `0.2095` would be 12.0035 degrees.
///
/// The dynamics are the standard ones - Barto, Sutton and Anderson 1983 - and the integration is
/// SEMI-IMPLICIT Euler: the position update uses the NEW velocity. Gym's default is explicit
/// Euler, which drifts over a long episode.
pub fn cartpoleStep(
    comptime T: type,
    state: CartpoleState(T),
    push: Push,
) CartpoleStep(T) {
    comptime requireFloat(T);
    const push_force: T = 10.0;
    const force: T = switch (push) {
        .left => -push_force,
        .right => push_force,
    };
    return cartpoleContinuousStep(T, state, force);
}

This works when the host function has a pure scalar form — one input struct to one output struct. A whole-tensor operation expressed over shapes and strides is a different algorithm from a kernel indexed by thread id, and sharing code between them gains nothing.

Every operation with a kernel is checked against its CPU twin on the same input, with a per-operation tolerance. Operations whose arithmetic cannot drift carry a bar of exactly zero — 9.10.

19. Gotchas#

Every entry here is something that produced a wrong answer without producing an error, during the writing of this library. They are collected because a trap you meet at three in the morning has to be findable, not discoverable by reading the section it happens to live in.

Each links to where it is explained.

19.1 Missing data#

  • The value under a missing slot is unspecified. A fill writes where it fills and nowhere else, so an unfilled slot keeps whatever it held. Read isValid before reading a value — 19.1 / 12.6
  • A fill can free the mask. Completing a column triggers the return to the cheap representation, so a defer gpa.free(col.valid.?) written before the fill unwraps a null — 12.6
  • An integer gap is a silent zero. A float gap is a loud NaN; an integer column has no NaN, so a mean over five slots where two were never measured is plausible and wrong — 12.4
  • A missing key matches nothing, not even another missing key. And the raw values under two gaps may well be equal — 12.9
  • A Series can be a VIEW. A column taken out of a matrix is strided, and reading its buffer directly walks a different column. Such a read gives 21 where the answer is 7 — 12.4

19.2 Edges and empties#

  • all of an empty tensor is TRUE and any is false. Forced by composition, not chosen — and getting it backwards passes every non-empty test — 9.8
  • arange excludes its stop; linspace asks. Same count, different spacing — 4.6
  • A trapezoid's endpoints count half. Five samples span four intervals, so a constant 1 integrates to 4 — 9.11
  • One sample integrates to zero, not to its own value — 9.11
  • The shifted-in rows and a partial window are missing, not zero. A zero reads as "no change" rather than "no data" — 12.11
  • n bins have n+1 edges, and the last is set to the bound rather than computed — 12.10

19.3 Numerics that lose the value#

  • Forming the 1 loses everything. log(1 + small) is zero once small falls under the epsilon of 1. It has cost three separate values here — log(softmax), softplus, and what logSumExp avoided by design. log1p and the max-subtraction are the fixes — 17.11
  • exp(-x) reaches zero near x = 103 in f32, so a value 110 below a row maximum softmaxes to exactly zero and its logarithm is -inf — 8.8
  • A product cannot have a zero tolerance. Multiplication is associative in real arithmetic and not in floating point — 9.10
  • Constant folding is a different machine. If a claim is about float or integer arithmetic, the operands must come from memory — a const is folded at full precision and proves nothing about the type you named
  • @constCast on a literal gives read-only memory. Fine to read from, aborts on a write — and a finite-difference probe writes — 17.11
  • Out of range in astype is an error, not a wrap. numpy wraps; Zig's @intFromFloat is undefined out of range, so the choice was forced — 4.7

19.4 Shapes and names#

  • stack grows the rank; concat grows an axis. Both take a list and an axis and the shapes look alike — 7.11
  • swapaxes returns a VIEW. Writing through it writes through to the original — 7.11
  • Precision is a COLUMN sum, recall a ROW sum. Swapping them gives plausible numbers on a symmetric matrix — 12.10
  • A duplicate join key multiplies rows, so a join can return more rows than either input — 12.9
  • Turns for angles that are drawn, radians for angles that are differentiated. d/dθ sin θ is cos θ only in radians, and the name carries the unit either way

addadd(self: *@This(), x: T) voidmethod
valuevalue(self: @This()) Tmethodtotal + compensation.
sumAllsumAll(comptime T: type, a: Tensor(T)) ThostCompensated (Neumaier).

prodAllprodAll(comptime T: type, a: Tensor(T)) Thost
cumsumcumsum(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostAlong the last axis. Rank 1 or 2.
anyNonzeroanyNonzero(comptime T: type, a: Tensor(T)) boolhost

wherewhere(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), mask: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), b: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostmask, a, b all broadcast to out.

modemode(comptime T: type, scratch: []T, a: Tensor(T)) Error!ThostMost common value; ties go to the SMALLEST, reproducibly.
SeriesSeries(comptime T: type) typehostA named column. `valid == null` means all present - no mask, no cost.

lenlen(self: Self) usizemethodEntries, present or not.
isValidisValid(self: Self, i: usize) boolmethodNo mask means everything is present.
ValidSumValidSum = structmethodSeries: what sumValid returns - the present values' total and their count.
sumValidsumValid(self: Self) ValidSummethodSKIPS the gaps. Raw sumAll adds zero for an integer gap and looks fine.
meanValidmeanValid(self: Self) ?TmethodNull, not NaN, when nothing is present.
fillMissingfillMissing(self: *Self, value: T) voidmethodA constant into every gap. The mask is then freed.
fillForwardfillForward(self: *Self) voidmethodLast real value forward. A LEADING gap stays missing - nothing to borrow.
fillBackwardfillBackward(self: *Self) voidmethodThe mirror. A trailing gap stays missing.

ColumnColumn = union(enum)hostA tagged union. `inline else` stamps one arm per type, not six copies.
deinitdeinit(self: Column) voidmethodGive back what init allocated: a masked array's values and mask, a network's or planner's tensors, a replay's rings.
lenlen(self: Column) usizemethodEntries, present or not.
namename(self: Column) []const u8methodThe column name, whatever its element type.
countValidcountValid(self: Column) usizemethodHow many entries are really there.
FrameFrame = structhostNamed columns, all one height. A ragged table is refused at the door.
initinit(gpa: Allocator) FramemethodConstruct: Rng.init(seed), Ctx.init(gpa, seed), and each layer's, network's and planner's init.

heightheight(self: *const Frame) usizemethodHow many rows - every column agrees.
addColumnaddColumn(self: *Frame, taken: Column) Error!voidmethodRefuses a wrong height AND a duplicate name: a lookup must not be ambiguous.
findfind(self: *const Frame, wanted: []const u8) ?usizemethodIndex of a named column, or null.

deinitdeinit(self: Self) voidmethodGive back what init allocated: a masked array's values and mask, a network's or planner's tensors, a replay's rings.

rowsrows(self: Self, g: usize) []const usizemethodThe row indices in one group.
CodeOrderCodeOrder = enumhostfirst_seen like pandas, or sorted. Required.
uniqueunique(comptime T: type, out: []T, a: Tensor(T)) Error!usizehostAscending, not first-seen.

RowPairRowPair = structhostOne joined row. `no_row` beats ?usize: dense array, tight loop.

JoinHowJoinHow = enumhostinner, left, right or outer.
joinRowsjoinRows(comptime K: type, gpa: Allocator, left_key: Series(K), right_key: Series(K), how: JoinHow) Error![]RowPairhostThe PAIRING without the gather. A missing key never matches, not even another.
SummarySummary(comptime T: type) typehostNamed fields rather than an array of eight.
AggregateAggregate = enumhostSeven that fit one pass. No variance or median stub that always errors.
needsFloatneedsFloat(self: Aggregate) boolmethodOnly mean does.
aggregateaggregate(comptime T: type, comptime how: Aggregate, gpa: Allocator, grouped: anytype, values: Series(T), name: []const u8) Error!Series(T)hostThe TYPE survives: sum of i32 is i32. A mean of i32 is a COMPILE error.
valueCountsvalueCounts(comptime T: type, out_values: []T, out_counts: []usize, scratch: []T, a: Tensor(T)) Error!usizehostDistinct values and frequencies, most common first. Returns the count.
logSumExplogSumExp(comptime T: type, a: Tensor(T)) Error!ThostSubtracts the max first, so exp cannot overflow. Direct: inf. This: finite.
logSumExpAxislogSumExpAxis(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), axis: usize) Error!voidhostPer row, so one saturating row does not affect its neighbours.
stdDevAxisstdDevAxis(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), axis: usize, ddof: Ddof) Error!voidhostThe square root of varianceAxis, without a second pass.
polyakUpdatepolyakUpdate(comptime T: type, target: Tensor(T), online: Tensor(T), follow: T) Error!voidhostAffine, not lerp: `follow = 1` is an exact copy. Not called `tau`.
addPointMassToGridaddPointMassToGrid(comptime T: type, bins: []T, grid_position: T, mass: T) voidhostSpread a point's mass onto the two grid bins around it.
symlogsymlog(comptime T: type, x: T) Thostsign(x) log(1 + |x|): squashes large magnitudes, the identity near zero.
symexpsymexp(comptime T: type, y: T) ThostThe inverse of symlog: sign(y) (exp(|y|) - 1).
CategoricalScalarCategoricalScalar(comptime T: type) typehostOne number predicted as a distribution over bins: two-hot encode, decode by the mean.
AxisAxis = enummethodCategoricalScalar's axis: symlog (TD-MPC2, BMPC) or identity (C51 / TD4 atoms).
checkcheck(self: Self) Error!voidmethodCategoricalScalar: refuse settings that describe no grid.
toAxistoAxis(self: Self, value: T) TmethodA value placed on the bins' axis.
fromAxisfromAxis(self: Self, axis_position: T) TmethodA position on the bins' axis taken back to a value.
binPositionbinPosition(self: Self, index: usize) TmethodWhere a bin sits on the axis.
encodeencode(self: Self, value: T, out: []T) Error!voidmethodThe two-hot target: two neighbouring bins, shared by closeness, summing to 1.
decodedecode(self: Self, probabilities: []const T) Error!TmethodA distribution over the bins read back as a number: the mean of the bins, off the axis.
encodeRowsencodeRows(self: Self, values: []const T, out: Tensor(T)) Error!voidmethodencode, one row per value.
decodeRowsdecodeRows(self: Self, probabilities: Tensor(T), out: []T) Error!voidmethoddecode, one value per row.
quantileBlendquantileBlend(self: Self, first: []const T, second: []const T, first_weight: T, out: []T) Error!voidmethodTwo distributions over the bins blended along their quantiles, reprojected: one point mass between two, never two bumps; the mean exactly the weighted mean.
twinTargettwinTarget(self: Self, first: []const T, second: []const T, lower_twin_weight: T, out: []T) Error!voidmethodTD4's target: the twin with the lower mean (weight 1), blended with the other along quantiles below 1.
twinTargetRowstwinTargetRows(self: Self, first: Tensor(T), second: Tensor(T), lower_twin_weight: T, out: Tensor(T)) Error!voidmethodtwinTarget for every row - the lower twin chosen row by row.
PushPush = enumhostleft or right.
categoricalcategorical(comptime T: type, logits: Tensor(T), rng: Rng, index: u32) Error!usizehostOne draw per sample. The max is subtracted, so logits of 800 work.
boundedIndexboundedIndex(rng: Rng, bound: usize, index: u32) Error!usizehostUniform without the modulo bias every tutorial ships.
affineaffine(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), gain: T, offset: T) Error!voidhosta * gain + offset: every scalar add, subtract, multiply, divide.
divFloordivFloor(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), b: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhost-7/2 is -4. `div` stays float-only so integers must choose.
divTruncdivTrunc(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), b: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhost-7/2 is -3. Both are correct; the caller says which.
divCeildivCeil(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), b: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostRounds up. What you want when sizing a buffer.
divExactdivExact(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), b: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostRefuses to round. @divExact is UNDEFINED when inexact; this errors.
modmod(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), b: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostSign follows the DIVISOR: -7 mod 3 is 2. Use this to wrap an index.
remrem(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), b: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostSign follows the DIVIDEND: -7 rem 3 is -1.
logSoftmaxRowslogSoftmaxRows(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostNever forms the softmax: a value 90 below the max gives -90, not -inf.
ComparisonComparison = enumhostNamed, so the call site reads as a sentence.

logicalXorlogicalXor(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), b: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostOne where exactly one is nonzero.

zeroszeros(comptime T: type, gpa: Allocator, shape: []const usize) Error!Tensor(T)hostalloc leaves GARBAGE - the common case gets a name.
onesones(comptime T: type, gpa: Allocator, shape: []const usize) Error!Tensor(T)hostAs zeros, filled with one.
fullfull(comptime T: type, gpa: Allocator, shape: []const usize, value: T) Error!Tensor(T)hostAs zeros, filled with a value.

bitwiseXorbitwiseXor(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), b: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostBit by bit.

moveAxismoveAxis(comptime T: type, a: Tensor(T), axis: usize, destination: usize) Error!Tensor(T)hostThe other axes keep their order.

loglog(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostNaN below zero, −inf at zero.
floorfloor(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhost
ceilceil(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhost

bmmbmm(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), b: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostBatched: (batch,m,k) @ (batch,k,n).

namedMatmulnamedMatmul(comptime T: type, comptime a_names: []const []const u8, comptime b_names: []const []const u8, out: Named(T, &.{ a_names[0], b_names[1] }), a: Named(T, a_names), b: Named(T, b_names)) Error!voidhostThe contracted axes must be the SAME axis, not just the same length.

diagonaldiagonal(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostRectangular too: min(rows, cols) entries.
TriangleTriangle = enumhostupper or lower.

choleskycholesky(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostLower-triangular L with L·Lᵀ = a. DomainError when not positive-definite.
determinantdeterminant(comptime T: type, a: Tensor(T), pivots: []usize) Error!ThostPivot sign times the diagonal. OVERWRITES `a`, as lu does.
ComplexNumberComplexNumber(comptime T: type) typehostextern, so an array is interleaved re/im.
addadd(a: Self, b: Self) Selfmethod
subsub(a: Self, b: Self) Selfmethod
mulmul(a: Self, b: Self) SelfmethodElementwise, not a matrix product.
magnitudemagnitude(a: Self) Tmethod
hessenberghessenberg(comptime T: type, a: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostZero below the first subdiagonal, from BOTH sides - one side would keep the shape and lose the eigenvalues.
eigeig(comptime T: type, out: []ComplexNumber(T), a: Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostGeneral real matrices, so eigenvalues may be complex. Real Schur form: a 2x2 block IS a conjugate pair. Values only, not vectors.

AdamAdam = structhostHyperparameters, defaulting to the paper's values.
adamStepadamStep(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), weight: Tensor(T), grad: Tensor(T), moment: Tensor(T), velocity: Tensor(T), hyper: Adam, step: usize) Error!voidhostmoment and velocity updated in place. step is 1-based, for the bias correction.
adamWStepadamWStep(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), weight: Tensor(T), grad: Tensor(T), moment: Tensor(T), velocity: Tensor(T), hyper: Adam, decay: T, step: usize) Error!voidhostDecay applied to the WEIGHT, not the gradient.
rmspropSteprmspropStep(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), weight: Tensor(T), grad: Tensor(T), mean_square: Tensor(T), rate: T, rho: T, epsilon: T) Error!voidhostAdam without the first moment or bias correction.
adagradStepadagradStep(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), weight: Tensor(T), grad: Tensor(T), accumulator: Tensor(T), rate: T, epsilon: T) Error!voidhostNever forgets, so the rate only shrinks.
clipByValueclipByValue(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), limit: T) Error!voidhostElementwise, so it CHANGES direction. See clipByNorm.
linearLearningRatelinearLearningRate(comptime T: type, step: usize, total: usize, base: T, lowest: T) ThostStraight-line decay - what PPO actually uses. On-policy data is thrown away each update, so late steps want a rate genuinely near zero, not near a floor.
linearOverFractionlinearOverFraction(comptime T: type, step: usize, total: usize) ThostThe fraction of training elapsed, so a caller annealing the rate AND the clip range uses ONE schedule rather than two that can drift apart.
cosineLearningRatecosineLearningRate(comptime T: type, step: usize, total: usize, base: T, lowest: T) Thostbase down to lowest, steepest in the middle.
warmupLearningRatewarmupLearningRate(comptime T: type, step: usize, warmup: usize, base: T) ThostLinear ramp. 0 at step 0, base at step warmup.
stepLearningRatestepLearningRate(comptime T: type, step: usize, every: usize, base: T, gamma: T) Error!ThostA staircase: flat, then a drop.
exponentialLearningRateexponentialLearningRate(comptime T: type, step: usize, base: T, decay: T) Thostbase * exp(-decay * step).
clipByNormclipByNorm(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), limit: T) Error!ThostScales the whole tensor. Returns the norm before clipping.

maxPool2dmaxPool2d(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), image: Tensor(T), size: usize) Error!voidhostNon-overlapping square windows. Partial trailing window dropped.
avgPool2davgPool2d(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), image: Tensor(T), size: usize) Error!voidhost
VarVar = u32;hostA handle into a Graph. An index, not a pointer.
SquashedDrawSquashedDraw = structhostWhat `squashedReparameterize` returns - the action for the critic, the log-probability for the entropy term.
GraphGraph(comptime T: type) typehostReverse-mode autograd. Eager forward, recorded backward.
initinit(gpa: Allocator) SelfmethodConstruct: Rng.init(seed), Ctx.init(gpa, seed), and each layer's, network's and planner's init.
useScratchAllocatoruseScratchAllocator(self: *Self, child: Allocator) voidmethodTakes backward's temporaries from a real allocator - for a graph reused over many passes.
deinitScratchdeinitScratch(self: *Self) voidmethodFrees those temporaries; pairs with useScratchAllocator.
parameterparameter(self: *Self, value: Tensor(T)) Error!VarmethodA value the graph differentiates with respect to.
constantconstant(self: *Self, value: Tensor(T)) Error!VarmethodA fixed value; accumulates no gradient.
valueOfvalueOf(self: *const Self, v: Var) Tensor(T)methodThe tensor behind a Var.
gradOfgradOf(self: *const Self, v: Var) Error!Tensor(T)methodDomainError for a constant.
addadd(self: *Self, a: Var, b: Var) Error!Varmethod
matmulmatmul(self: *Self, a: Var, b: Var) Error!VarmethodRank 2. Compensated inner sum.
subsub(self: *Self, a: Var, b: Var) Error!Varmethod
RowReductionRowReduction = enummethodWhich fold `reduceRows` applies. `mean` is composed from `sum` and a scale, not a third op - two implementations of one derivative is how they drift.
reduceRowsreduceRows(self: *Self, a: Var, kind: RowReduction) Error!VarmethodFold each row to one number - sum, max or mean. The tape had no axis reduction, so this was open-coded as a matmul-with-ones in five places.
squaredRowNormsquaredRowNorm(self: *Self, a: Var) Error!Varmethod`sum(x^2)` per row - the shape a gradient penalty is measured in.
rowDotrowDot(self: *Self, a: Var, b: Var) Error!Varmethod`sum(a*b)` per row. A cosine similarity when both sides are unit-length, which is what an encoder reward assumes and normalisation is responsible for.
minmin(self: *Self, a: Var, b: Var) Error!VarmethodElementwise minimum on the tape - the pessimism TD3 and DroQ are built on. The whole gradient goes to the winner; ties go left, never half to each.
mulmul(self: *Self, a: Var, b: Var) Error!VarmethodElementwise, not a matrix product.
detachdetach(self: *Self, a: Var) Error!VarmethodGraph op: the input's value with no gradient through it - a stop-gradient.
relurelu(self: *Self, a: Var) Error!Varmethod
sigmoidsigmoid(self: *Self, a: Var) Error!Varmethod
tanhtanh(self: *Self, a: Var) Error!Varmethod
tanhIntoRangetanhIntoRange(self: *Self, x: Var, low: T, high: T) Error!VarmethodGraph: low + (high - low) * (tanh(x) + 1) / 2 - an output held smoothly inside an interval.
expexp(self: *Self, a: Var) Error!Varmethod
loglog(self: *Self, a: Var) Error!VarmethodNaN below zero, −inf at zero.
softplussoftplus(self: *Self, a: Var) Error!VarmethodIts OWN node: log(1+exp(x)) overflows at x=89 in f32. Backward is sigmoid.
eluelu(self: *Self, a: Var, alpha: T) Error!VarmethodA real node: a branch is not a composition. Backward reads the INPUT.
activateactivate(self: *Self, x: Var, activation: Activation) Error!VarmethodGraph: a value through an Activation.
mishmish(self: *Self, x: Var) Error!Varmethodx * tanh(softplus(x)) - a composition once softplus is a node.
silusilu(self: *Self, x: Var) Error!Varmethodx·sigmoid(x), also called swish.
gelugelu(self: *Self, x: Var) Error!Varmethodtanh approximation.
gluglu(self: *Self, x: Var) Error!Varmethodslice * sigmoid(slice), composed of graph operations.
swigluswiglu(self: *Self, x: Var) Error!VarmethodThe same, gated by SiLU. Every recent transformer uses it.
GateGate = enummethodIn a cell, one gate's two matrices and its bias; in a gated unit, which nonlinearity.
squashedReparameterizesquashedReparameterize(self: *Self, mean: Var, log_std: Var, noise: Tensor(T)) Error!SquashedDrawmethodSAC's reparameterised action AND its log-prob, on the tape. The tanh correction uses the softplus form: the textbook one is log(0) at a saturated action.
categoricalLogProbcategoricalLogProb(self: *Self, logits: Var, actions: []const usize) Error!VarmethodPer-sample discrete log-probability on the tape. reduces to a scalar and PPO needs one per sample - a mean cannot be un-meaned.
gradientOfgradientOf(self: *Self, output: Var, input: Var) Error!VarmethodA gradient AS A GRAPH NODE, so it can be squared, summed and differentiated again. What a gradient penalty needs, and what `backward` cannot give.
adaptiveLayerNormadaptiveLayerNorm(self: *Self, x: Var, conditioning_gain: Var, conditioning_bias: Var, epsilon: T) Error!VarmethodLayerNorm whose gain and bias come from a conditioning signal - how a timestep or a goal reaches a whole layer. The gain is `1 + c`, so zero is the identity.
scaledDotProductAttentionscaledDotProductAttention(self: *Self, query: Var, key: Var, value: Var, score_scale: T) Error!Varmethod`softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V`, composed from tape ops so there is no new backward. The `1/sqrt(d)` is the part people drop, and dropping it makes wider models train worse.
EncoderWeightsEncoderWeights = structmethodOne block's six projections, named - because six `Var`s in a row is six chances to swap two, and swapping `wq` with `wk` computes attention backwards and still trains.
encoderBlockencoderBlock(self: *Self, x: Var, w: EncoderWeights, score_scale: T, epsilon: T) Error!VarmethodOne PRE-norm transformer block. Pre-norm leaves a path from input to output through no normalisation, so gradient reaches the first layer undiminished.
klGaussianDiagklGaussianDiag(self: *Self, mean: Var, log_std: Var, reference_mean: Tensor(T), reference_log_std: Tensor(T)) Error!VarmethodThe EXACT KL between two diagonal Gaussians. KL(new||old) - the direction is the point, and swapping it computes something real, different, and silent.
copyToEveryRowcopyToEveryRow(self: *Self, value: Var, row_count: usize) Error!VarmethodGraph: a [1, d] value copied to every row - exact, its gradient summed back.
copyToEveryColumncopyToEveryColumn(self: *Self, column: Var, column_count: usize) Error!VarmethodGraph: a [rows, 1] column copied to every column - exact, its gradient summed back.
diagGaussianEntropydiagGaussianEntropy(self: *Self, log_std: Var) Error!VarmethodGraph: a diagonal Gaussian's entropy per row, DiagGaussian.entropy's twin; gradient 1 per log std.
diagGaussianLogProbdiagGaussianLogProb(self: *Self, mean: Var, log_std: Var, actions: Tensor(T)) Error!VarmethodA diagonal Gaussian's log-density ON THE TAPE - the missing link between a network that outputs mean/log_std and a loss that can be descended.
crossEntropycrossEntropy(self: *Self, logits: Var, labels: []const usize) Error!VarmethodLabels are a []usize, not a Var: they have no gradient.
softCrossEntropysoftCrossEntropy(self: *Self, logits: Var, targets: Var) Error!VarmethodGraph op: mean cross-entropy of logits against soft targets.
softmaxRowssoftmaxRows(self: *Self, a: Var) Error!VarmethodRank 2. The row maximum is subtracted.
simNormsimNorm(self: *Self, a: Var, group: usize) Error!VarmethodGraph op: SimNorm with a group size.
layerNormRowslayerNormRows(self: *Self, a: Var, epsilon: T) Error!VarmethodRank 2, population variance, epsilon is a parameter.
conv2dconv2d(self: *Self, input: Var, kernel: Var, stride: [2]usize, pad: [2]usize) Error!VarmethodCross-correlation with stride and zero padding, per axis. Rank 2.
sliceslice(self: *Self, a: Var, axis: usize, start: usize, len: usize) Error!VarmethodA window. Shares storage.
concatconcat(self: *Self, a: Var, b: Var, axis: usize) Error!VarmethodDifferentiable. The backward is the slice, read backwards.
embeddingembedding(self: *Self, table: Var, rows: []const usize) Error!VarmethodOn the graph. Gradient is a scatter-add.
transposetranspose(self: *Self, a: Var) Error!VarmethodExchanges two axes.
gatherColumnsgatherColumns(self: *Self, input: Var, columns: []const usize) Error!Varmethodout[r][k] = table[r][columns[k]]; on the graph a product with a 0/1 selection matrix - exact, its gradient zero for the unchosen.
scalescale(self: *Self, a: Var, factor: T) Error!VarmethodRuntime factor, so not a zip.
dropoutdropout(self: *Self, a: Var, rate: T, rng: Rng) Error!VarmethodInverted. Mask drawn once and stored; see resampleDropout.
resampleDropoutresampleDropout(self: *Self, rng: Rng) voidmethodFresh masks, each node from its own generator split. Once per step.
mseLossmseLoss(self: *Self, a: Var, target: Var) Error!VarmethodReturns a scalar. Shapes must match exactly.
preActivationPenaltypreActivationPenalty(self: *Self, pre_activation: Var) Error!VarmethodMean over rows of the sum of relu(u - 1)^2 + relu(-u - 1)^2: zero inside [-1, 1], no kink at 0.
backwardbackward(self: *Self, loss: Var) Error!voidmethodSeeds 1 into a single-element value and walks the tape back.
recomputerecompute(self: *Self) Error!voidmethodReplays the tape forward. Leaves keep whatever was written.
checkGradientcheckGradient(self: *Self, loss: Var, param: Var, h: T) Error!TmethodWorst gap against a central finite difference. Restores the model.
numericalGradnumericalGrad(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), x: Tensor(T), step: T, evaluator: anytype) Error!voidhostCentral difference for losses the TAPE cannot see. Owns the restore-exactly bookkeeping, which is where the mistakes live.
numericalGradWorstnumericalGradWorst(comptime T: type, gpa: Allocator, analytic: Tensor(T), x: Tensor(T), step: T, evaluator: anytype) Error!ThostThe same sweep reporting one worst-case ratio instead of a tensor.

stepParametersstepParameters(comptime T: type, graph: *Graph(T), weights: []const Tensor(T), parameters: []const Var, learning_rate: T) Error!voidhostDescend every parameter once. The one place the optimiser lives, which is what makes swapping SGD for Adam a small change.
maskedMeanmaskedMean(comptime T: type, values: []const T, keep: []const bool) Error!ThostMean over the kept entries. An empty mask is an ERROR - returning zero for nothing-selected is wrong in the direction that hides.
l2NormalizeRowsl2NormalizeRows(comptime T: type, out: Tensor(T), a: Tensor(T), epsilon: T) Error!voidhostScale each row to unit length. Without it ASE's encoder reward stops being a cosine and the diversity objective becomes a magnitude contest.
dtwDistancedtwDistance(comptime T: type, gpa: Allocator, a: Tensor(T), b: Tensor(T)) Error!ThostDynamic Time Warping: the same motion at a different SPEED costs zero, which frame-by-frame comparison cannot say. A metric, not a loss - no gradient.
NoiseScheduleNoiseSchedule = enumhost`linear` or `cosine`. Linear destroys the signal early, so half the model's capacity goes to steps that are already noise; cosine keeps it alive longer.
betaSchedulebetaSchedule(comptime T: type, betas: []T, kind: NoiseSchedule) Error!voidhostHow much variance each diffusion step adds - a statement about where the model spends its capacity.
alphasCumprodalphasCumprod(comptime T: type, out: []T, betas: []const T) Error!voidhostThe cumulative signal fraction. Computed ONCE - recomputing the product inside a sampling loop makes generation quadratic in the step count.
addNoiseaddNoise(comptime T: type, x0: T, noise: T, alpha_bar: T) ThostThe forward process. The two coefficients square to one, so variance is preserved at every timestep - which is what lets ONE model handle them all.
epsilonFromX0epsilonFromX0(comptime T: type, x_t: T, x0: T, alpha_bar: T) ThostRecover the noise from a prediction of the clean sample. Models predict one of the two and the sampling loops need the other.
sinusoidalEmbeddingsinusoidalEmbedding(comptime T: type, out: []T, position: T, max_period: T) Error!voidhostA timestep or position as sinusoids at geometrically spaced frequencies - far apart where behaviour should differ, close where it should not.
classifierFreeGuidanceclassifierFreeGuidance(comptime T: type, conditional: T, unconditional: T, strength: T) ThostExtrapolate a conditional prediction away from an unconditional one. Both 0 and 1 are fixed points; only beyond 1 does anything happen.
emaUpdateemaUpdate(comptime T: type, shadow: Tensor(T), live: Tensor(T), decay: T) Error!voidhost`polyakUpdate` under the name its other users know. Takes DECAY, the large number, where polyak takes follow, the small one - they differ by exactly 1.
x0FromEpsilonx0FromEpsilon(comptime T: type, x_t: T, epsilon: T, alpha_bar: T) ThostThe clean sample from a noise prediction - the partner of `epsilonFromX0`.
diffusionReverseStepdiffusionReverseStep(comptime T: type, x_t: T, epsilon: T, alpha_bar_t: T, alpha_bar_prev: T, eta: T, fresh_noise: T) ThostOne reverse step. DDPM and DDIM are ONE update with a parameter - `eta` is how much fresh noise enters, zero deterministic, one the original chain.
clipGradNormclipGradNorm(comptime T: type, graph: *const Graph(T), parameters: []const Var, max_norm: T) Error!ThostONE norm over all parameters - per-tensor clipping changes the DIRECTION.
saveTensorssaveTensors(comptime T: type, gpa: Allocator, out: *ArrayList(u8), names: []const []const u8, tensors: []const Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostLittle-endian, explicit widths. Contiguous only.
saveParameterssaveParameters(comptime T: type, gpa: Allocator, out: *ArrayList(u8), graph: *const Graph(T), parameters: []const Var) Error!voidhostA trained network to bytes. Named p0, p1 - so the ORDER must match.
loadTensorsloadTensors(comptime T: type, bytes: []const u8, names: []const []const u8, into: []const Tensor(T)) Error!voidhostInto tensors the caller holds, matched by name.
loadParametersloadParameters(comptime T: type, gpa: Allocator, bytes: []const u8, graph: *const Graph(T), parameters: []const Var) Error!voidhostBack into a network of the same shape. loadTensors refuses a mismatch.
gradientgradient(comptime T: type, out: []T, values: []const T, spacing: T) Error!voidhostCentral inside, one-sided at the ends.
trapezoidtrapezoid(comptime T: type, values: []const T, spacing: T) Error!ThostExact for any straight line.
interpinterp(comptime T: type, out: []T, at: []const T, xs: []const T, ys: []const T) Error!voidhostClamps outside the range rather than extrapolating.
dftdft(comptime T: type, out: []ComplexNumber(T), input: []const ComplexNumber(T), exponent_sign: T) Error!voidhostO(n²), any length. The reference `fft` is checked against.
fftfft(comptime T: type, data: []ComplexNumber(T), exponent_sign: T) Error!voidhostRadix-2, in place, power-of-two. 630× faster than dft at 4096.
ifftifft(comptime T: type, data: []ComplexNumber(T)) Error!voidhostThe whole 1/n lives here.
fftFreqfftFreq(comptime T: type, out: []T, spacing: T) Error!voidhostSecond half is negative frequencies.
rfftrfft(comptime T: type, out: []ComplexNumber(T), input: []const T, scratch: []ComplexNumber(T)) Error!voidhostReal input, n/2 + 1 bins. Half the transform, not a full one halved.
imdctDirectimdctDirect(comptime T: type, out: []T, coefficients: []const T) Error!voidhostO(N²), any N: 2N samples from N coefficients. The reference `imdct` is checked against.
imdctimdct(comptime T: type, out: []T, coefficients: []const T, scratch: []ComplexNumber(T)) Error!voidhostN a power of two: a DCT-IV through one N/2-point fft, unfolded. Overlapped blocks give back N/2 times the signal.
ConvModeConvMode = enumhostfull, same, valid. Each is a window onto full.
outputLenoutputLen(self: ConvMode, a: usize, v: usize) usizemethodOutputs a mode produces. `length` is reserved.
convolveconvolve(comptime T: type, out: []T, a: []const T, v: []const T, extent: ConvMode) Error!voidhostFlips the kernel.
correlatecorrelate(comptime T: type, out: []T, a: []const T, v: []const T, extent: ConvMode) Error!voidhostDoes not flip the kernel.
expectReferenceTableMatchesexpectReferenceTableMatches(html: []const u8, source: []const u8) !voidhostTests a tutorial's table against a source's public names.

Source: src/zimrnum.zig. Design and status: src/notes/zimrnum_plan.md. Engine documentation: src/web/readme.html.
